transcript.text: gas hob keeps clickin on its own since i cleand it, stops then starts agen. drivin me mad. pls help

That's a really common one after cleaning, and it's usually water, not a broken part. The most likely causes, in order:
1. Moisture or cleaner got into the ignition switches behind the knobs. Water there completes the switch, so the hob thinks a knob is being pushed and fires the igniters. As it dries and shifts, it stops and starts, exactly like you're seeing.
2. A burner cap or the white igniter tip is still wet or greasy, or a cap isn't sitting square, so the spark misbehaves.
3. Less likely: a knob is stuck slightly pushed in, or an ignition switch has failed. What to do:
1. Stop the clicking safely: make sure all gas knobs are off, then switch off the hob's electric supply. It's usually a plug in the cupboard below or a switched spur on the wall. The burners still work if you light them with a match, but don't cook with it while it's misbehaving if you'd rather not.
2. Pull the knobs straight off (they usually just pull off). Wipe and dry the knobs and the area around the spindles, and check none feels stuck or doesn't spring back. A stuck knob points to cause 3.
3. Lift off the burner caps and crowns, dry them thoroughly, gently wipe the igniter tips dry, then re-seat each cap so it sits flat.
4. Leave it switched off to dry properly, ideally 24 hours, even up to 48 if it got soaked. Leaving the knobs off helps air get in. Then switch the power back on. If the clicking has gone, it was moisture and nothing needs replacing. If it still clicks after a good couple of days drying, the ignition switch or spark unit has probably been damaged. That sits inside the hob near the gas controls, so it's a job for a Gas Safe registered engineer rather than something to take apart yourself. And if you ever smell gas, turn it off, open windows and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999. To help narrow it down: is it clicking at every burner at once, or just one? And did it get very wet, or sprayed with cleaner, around the knobs?
not sure which burner, its one or more i think. yeah i sloshed loads of water around and took the caps off. i unplugged the hob under the sink and its stopped clicking now. no gas smell btw

Good, that's the right move, and no gas smell is reassuring. With that much water sloshed around, it's probably moisture in the ignition switches behind the knobs. It's stopped because the power is off, so the real test is what happens once it has dried out. 1. Leave it unplugged for 24 to 48 hours. Pull the knobs off if you can, so air gets to the spindles.
2. Make sure the burner caps and igniter tips are dry, and that each cap sits flat when you put it back.
3. Plug it back in. If it stays quiet, it was just water and nothing needs replacing. If it still clicks on its own after a proper dry-out, the water has probably damaged an ignition switch or the spark unit. That's a job for a Gas Safe engineer. In the meantime you can still light the burners with a match. To stop it happening again, clean around the knobs with a well wrung-out cloth rather than lots of water. Don't spray cleaner straight onto the hob near the controls; spray it onto the cloth instead. Is there anything else I can help with?

candidates: Moisture or cleaning fluid in the ignition switches under the knobs (high)
Wet, greasy or misaligned burner cap or igniter electrode letting the spark track (medium)
A control knob stuck pushed in, or a faulty ignition switch/spark unit (low)
